conventions.convention: Decision correctness is required only on disjoint yes/no promise sets; search correctness requires a witness in the declared relation only on its promise domain.
Input encoding is injective, and input size is the encoded string length; the hidden encoding labels the instance without granting readable input access.

Each oracle function is total on its complete address domain. One coherent XOR invocation counts as one query regardless of reply width; its inverse is the same ordinary query, while controlled access requires an explicit capability and charge.

At fixed encoded length and public data, the quantum protocol, initial state, nonoracle operations, instruments, branch rules, and output rules are independent of the hidden instance. Additional instance-dependent access must be explicitly supplied and charged.

Finite instrument branches use observed outcome labels, retain density states only on positive-probability branches, and sum terminal diagonal weights over all unmeasured wires. Zero-probability descendants contribute no output weight.
Bounded error means success probability at least 2/3 on every promised instance, rather than an input-distribution average.
Worst-case quantum query cost maximizes over promised instances and all measurement branches; an empty length-specific promise has cost zero. Expected query cost is a separate coordinate.

Expected query cost is the supremum of finite-prefix expected call counts. No probability measure on infinite histories is presumed; the round-end identification assumes a fixed finite elementary-step bound per padded round.

Nonoracle elementary gates, preparation, measurements, classical processing, and oracle calls have separate resource coordinates; classical bit cost counts transitions of a declared fixed-alphabet multitape machine.

load_bearing.statement: At each encoded length n and declared public data p, a quantum query algorithm is a finite circuit protocol fixed independently of the hidden instance. A T-query algorithm makes at most T designated oracle calls on every execution branch for every promised instance.

For the specified finite execution tree of unitary and finite instrument nodes, the terminal output weights form a normalized probability law, and every predicate-selected acceptance probability lies in [0,1].

Each encoded promised instance selects a total function from a(n)-bit addresses to b(n)-bit replies. Its standard quantum query is the coherent XOR action, and one invocation is one query regardless of output width.

A decision task has disjoint yes/no promise sets. A search task has a promise domain D and witness relation R, requiring a witness w with (z,w) in R for each z in D. Neither imposes correctness outside its promise.
Expected query cost on a fixed promised input is sup over M in the natural numbers of E[C_M], where C_M counts calls in the normalized finite length-M execution-prefix experiment.

Under the stated promise-preserving decision or computable search maps, exact admissible target initialization and witness lifting, and direct target access or exact charged query simulation, composition preserves the target solver's per-instance correctness. Source query bounds are T or sT with no additional initialization/lifting queries, and u+T+v or u+sT+v with the stated additive overhead.

published_dependencies.used_for: Normalized finite execution-prefix spaces and their nonnegative weights.
Treating each bounded finite-prefix call count as a finite real random variable.
Finite weighted-sum expectations and monotonicity of prefix expected query counts.
Summing child weights, preserving prefix marginals, and interchanging terminal leaf and output sums.
Finite-prefix normalization and finite execution-tree normalization.
Disjoint decision promise sets and absence of off-promise correctness obligations.
Positivity of density operators, unitary state updates, and terminal diagonal weights.
Root-linear-first adjoint identities in unitary density-state updates.
Meaning of the explicitly declared unitary execution-tree edges.
The unitary identity U-adjoint times U equals identity.
Trace-one state normalization and terminal probabilities as sums of computational-basis diagonal entries.
Preservation of trace under unitary conjugation.
Finite fair-bit random-tape semantics and the distinction between branch bounds and expected cost.
The declared multitape transition model for classical bit costs.
Total polynomial-time decision many-one reductions preserving both promise sides.
The example's direct calculation that two Hadamard gates compose to identity.

seams_checked.note: The base promise model supplies terminal conventions; intermediate instruments are explicitly added locally. Uniformity and resource coordinates remain separately declared.
The total XOR oracle, involutive inverse, and separation of black-box access from circuit implementation are preserved.
Big-endian ordering, orthonormal product bases, and the one-dimensional zero-qubit register agree with the suppliers.
The root pairing is linear first; Dirac notation reverses its arguments, consistently with the diagonal probability calculation.
Wire order, later-on-left composition, and separate elementary/query costs are used faithfully.
Instrument normalization and conditional-state density are applied only to density inputs and positive-probability branches.
Standard XOR calls, explicit preparation gates, and controlled-phase capability retain their distinct charges.
Promise definitions, truth-table input length, terminal output laws, and preparation-inclusive gate counts match the cited interfaces.
Classical lower bounds fix oracle-only access; unbounded rank collection uses finite-prefix expected cost separately from the capped procedure.
Arithmetic and reconstruction claims use the declared multitape bit-transition coordinate separately from gates and controlled calls.
Finite query bounds include candidate verification; BBHT expected cost uses finite prefixes and remains distinct from gate and preprocessing costs.
Declared preparation, inverse, reflection, and measurement accesses are charged separately; unbounded procedures use finite-prefix expected cost.
Controlled-power and repeated-controlled-call modes are explicitly declared, with separate query and classical postprocessing coordinates.
The local Boolean search model preserves hidden-input independence, per-instance 2/3 correctness, and worst-branch query accounting.
The local oracle-only specialization preserves finite instrument semantics and explicitly distinguishes one algorithm's cost from minimization over feasible algorithms.
Normal-form and adversary uses retain the worst-branch query coordinate, fixed bounded-error convention, and separate nonoracle synthesis costs.
